\begin{bankq}[id=SA02-P1-PHY-S3-Q01, source={Score Advanced - Test 02 (13 May 2021)}, paper=1, qno=1, type=numerical, subtopic={Vernier and screw gauge}, answer={2.66}, answer_src=solved, working={Least count 0.01 cm gives side 1.01 cm; density 2.736/1.0303=2.66 g/cm3 (3 significant figures)}, difficulty=4, diff_parts={K1 S2 I1 C0 F1}, diff_note={concepts: density with vernier reading | steps: least count; reading; significant figures}]

\begin{bankq}[id=SA06-P2-PHY-S3-Q08, source={Score Advanced - Test 06 (04 Sep 2021)}, paper=2, qno=8, type=numerical, subtopic={Vernier and screw gauge}, answer={4}, answer_src=solved, working={2(0.005/0.5)+0.005/0.25=2+2=4 percent}, difficulty=6, diff_parts={K2 S1 I2 C1 F1}, diff_note={concepts: percentage error in Young's modulus, vernier and screw gauge | steps: least count 0.5/100=0.005 mm; Y proportional to 1/(d\^{}2 l)}, also_in={Score Advanced - Test 28 (27 Apr 2024) P1 Q6}]

For a load M = 2.5 kg, an extension $\ell$ = 0.25 mm in the length of the wire is observed. Quantities d and $\ell$ are measured using a screw gauge and a micrometer, respectively. They have the same pitch of 0.5 mm. The number of divisions on their circular scale is 100. The length of wire, acceleration due to gravity and mass M are known exactly. The percentage error in measurement of the Young's modulus is\underline{\hspace{2cm}}
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=SA07-P1-PHY-S3-Q08, source={Score Advanced - Test 07 (16 Apr 2023)}, paper=1, qno=8, type=numerical, subtopic={Vernier and screw gauge}, answer={6.04}, answer_src=key, difficulty=7, diff_parts={K2 S2 I2 C1 F1}, diff_note={concepts: diameter from a screw gauge with zero error, vernier and screw gauge | steps: pitch 1 mm; zero error +4 divisions; reading}]
In a screw gauge whose least count is 0.005 mm, when no object is present and the screw gauge gap is completely closed the 4$^{\text{th}}$ division on its circular scale coincides with the reference line on main scale reading zero. Now a wire is placed in it to measure its diameter, the reading on the main scale advances by 6 divisions, whereas the circular scale reading becomes 3 times to the corresponding reading when no object was placed. If there are 200 divisions on circular scale, then find the diameter of wire in mm.
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=SA08-P1-PHY-S3-Q04, source={Score Advanced - Test 08 (22 Apr 2023)}, paper=1, qno=4, type=numerical, subtopic={Vernier and screw gauge}, answer={1}, answer_src=key, difficulty=9, diff_parts={K3 S2 I2 C2 F1}, diff_note={concepts: spring compression from vernier readings, vernier and screw gauge, least count of the vernier | steps: least count of the vernier; compression under the force; proportional change for the shorter spring}]
A vernier calliper has no zero error, one main scale division = 1 mm and 9 main scale division = 10 vernier scale divisions. A spring is held between jaws without exerting force on jaws. Main scale reading is 3.4 cm and 5$^{\text{th}}$ vernier scale division coincides with a main division. When Jaws are pressed by force of 10 N on both sides, main scale reading remains 3.4 cm, but 1$^{\text{st}}$ division of vernier scale coincides with a main scale division. Now spring is removed, cut into two pieces and when one part is inserted between jaws without any force, main scale reading = 1.1 cm and 5$^{\text{th}}$ vernier scale division coincides with a main scale. If we apply force of 30 N on both the jaws, main scale reading remains 1.1 cm and x vernier scale division coincides with a main scale division. Find x.
\end{bankq}

\begin{bankq}[id=SA18-P1-PHY-S1-Q01, source={Score Advanced - Test 18 (27 May 2023)}, paper=1, qno=1, type=multi, subtopic={Units and dimensions}, answer={A,B,C,D}, answer_src=key, difficulty=7, diff_parts={K3 S1 I2 C1 F1}, diff_note={concepts: relations between two systems of units, units and dimensions, scale factors for velocity acceleration and force | steps: scale factors for velocity acceleration and force; derive others}]
The velocity, acceleration and force in two systems of units are related to each other as under\par
(i) $v'=\frac{\alpha^2}{\beta}v$\quad (ii) $a'=(\alpha\beta)a$\quad (iii) $F'=\left(\frac{1}{\alpha\beta}\right)F$\par
where, all the primed symbols belong to one system of units and the unprimed symbols belong to the other system of units. Here $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are dimensionless constants. Which of the following is / are correct ?
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{The standard of length in each of these two systems are related to each other as $\ell'=\frac{\alpha^3}{\beta^3}\ell$.}
\opt{B}{The standard of mass in each of these two systems are related to each other as $m'=\left(\frac{1}{\alpha^2\beta^2}\right)m$.}
\opt{C}{The standard of time in each of these two systems are related to each other as $t'=\left(\frac{\alpha}{\beta^2}\right)t$.}
\opt{D}{The standard of momentum in each of these two systems are related to each other as $p'=\left(\frac{1}{\beta^3}\right)p$.}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}

When an object is placed between jaws, main scale reading is at 45$^{th}$ division and vernier coincides is at 5$^{th}$ division mark. What is the true length (in cm) of object ?
\end{bankq}
